about: Real-world video and photo sources for documentary b-roll, with search APIs and licence notes. Human-readable version: docs/assets/footage-library.md. Downloader: node engine/footage.js fetch <query> --source <id>. 'auth' none = works from this box without any account. Licence notes verified 2026-10-12 against the pages in 'evidence'.
policy: Ship only public domain, CC0, or US Government works (and Pexels/Pixabay under their own licences, never redistributed as-is). Never CC BY-NC / ND. Check every item: agency pages can carry third-party copyrighted material, and archive.org PD marks set by arbitrary uploaders are not evidence.

sources.name: NASA Image and Video Library
sources.files: ~orig (master, often 4K ProRes/H.264, up to several GB), ~large (1080p/4K H.264), ~medium, ~small, ~mobile
sources.licence: Public domain in the US (NASA media is generally not subject to copyright).
sources.restrictions: NASA insignia/logotype are not PD; no implied endorsement; identifiable people need permission for commercial use; third-party material is marked and needs its owner's permission; no NFTs; no NASA attribution of AI-generated output.
sources.credit: NASA (centre, e.g. NASA/JSC) as the source
strengths: ISS night passes, cities at night, aurora

sources.name: NASA Goddard Scientific Visualization Studio
sources.licence: Public domain (NASA); each page lists credits, and some data layers (e.g. commercial imagery) carry their own terms.
sources.credit: NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio (+ page credits)

sources.name: NOAA (NESDIS, Hurricane Hunters, Photo Library, NWS)

api.search: No unified video API. NESDIS and Hurricane Hunter videos are mirrored on Wikimedia Commons (search '<topic> NESDIS' / 'NOAA'); GOES imagery via NASA SVS; photos via the NOAA Photo Library site.

sources.licence: Public domain (US Government work) unless marked otherwise.
sources.credit: NOAA (office, e.g. NOAA NESDIS / NOAA AOC)
sources.downloader: --source noaa (Commons search with 'NOAA' appended) or --source commons
strengths: GOES hurricane loops with 'NO TEXT' versions

sources.name: DVIDS (Defense Visual Information Distribution Service)
sources.licence: US DoW visual information is generally public domain (works of government employees); some items are owned by non-DoW parties.
sources.restrictions: Display the disclaimer 'The appearance of U.S. Department of War (DoW) visual information does not imply or constitute DoW endorsement.'; no implied endorsement; military names, insignia and seals need permission for commercial use (commercial users are asked to obscure distinctive markings); privacy/publicity rights of people shown remain.
sources.credit: DVIDS / unit name, photographer or videographer
sources.downloader: --source dvids (with DVIDS_API_KEY). Without a key: thousands of DVIDS videos are mirrored on Commons as PD-USGov-Military; use --source commons and a DVIDS-style query.

sources.name: US National Archives (NARA) Catalog
sources.licence: Most federal records are public domain; check each record's 'useRestriction' (some donated films are copyrighted).
sources.restrictions: API terms: display 'This product uses the National Archives Catalog API'; do not cache/store API responses; no NARA logos.
sources.credit: National Archives and Records Administration (record NAID)
sources.downloader: --source nara (with NARA_API_KEY). Without a key: NARA's own uploads to archive.org (identifiers gov.archives.*) via --source archive.

sources.name: Library of Congress

api.auth: none (rate limited; no deep paging past 100k)

sources.licence: Varies per item: use only items whose rights advisory says 'No known restrictions on publication' or public domain.
sources.downloader: --source loc (licence read from the item's rights_advisory)

sources.name: Prelinger Archives (on archive.org)
sources.licence: Per film. Many downloads carry the Creative Commons Public Domain Dedication (licenseurl .../publicdomain/), which does not expire; Prelinger states plainly that 'while some Prelinger films are in the public domain, many are not'. Use only items whose licenseurl is a PD dedication/mark; otherwise ask Prelinger or license via Getty Images.
sources.restrictions: PD films can contain copyrighted elements (music, inserted footage). Transfers 2000-2022 are compressed NTSC (SD); 2023+ are better. Credit is not required but welcome.
sources.downloader: --source prelinger (keeps only PD-marked items in the prelinger collection)

sources.name: FedFlix and agency uploads on archive.org
sources.licence: US Government works (public domain); items with identifiers gov.* come from NARA/NTIS/agencies.
sources.credit: US Government film (agency), via Internet Archive / Public.Resource.Org
sources.downloader: --source fedflix, or --source archive (gov.* identifiers are trusted)

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons (video)

api.auth: none; send a descriptive User-Agent (generic agents get HTTP 429)

sources.licence: Per file (extmetadata LicenseShortName). Keep only Public domain / PD-USGov-* / CC0. CC BY and CC BY-SA need attribution (and share-alike) and are skipped unless --allow-by.
sources.restrictions: Upload servers rate-limit range reads; the downloader fetches the VP9 transcode whole and trims locally.
sources.credit: Author per file page + 'via Wikimedia Commons'

sources.name: US Government agency b-roll (direct)
sources.url: e.g. https://www.energy.gov/media-library , https://www.usgs.gov/media , https://www.nps.gov/subjects/digital/ , https://www.fema.gov/multimedia-library , https://www.bep.gov (Bureau of Engraving and Printing) , https://www.army.mil , https://www.af.mil , https://www.navy.mil

api.search: No common API; most agencies post to DVIDS, YouTube (not downloadable here), Flickr (PD or 'United States Government Work' mark) and Commons.

sources.licence: Works of federal employees are public domain (17 U.S.C. 105). Contractor-made material (national labs run by contractors, e.g. LLNL, LANL) and agency pages with third-party content can be copyrighted: check the page.
sources.downloader: manual: save the file + write a provenance JSON with the same fields as engine/footage.js produces

sources.name: Pexels Videos

api.auth: free API key in PEXELS_API_KEY (Authorization header)

sources.licence: Pexels licence: free for commercial use, modification allowed, attribution optional.
sources.restrictions: Do not sell unaltered copies; do not redistribute on stock/wallpaper platforms; no endorsement implied by identifiable people/brands; no use in trademarks. => Use inside edited films only; never commit or share the raw files (assets/footage/clips is git-ignored).
strengths: modern stock: typing hands, server rooms, drones, city timelapses, crowds

sources.name: Pixabay Videos
sources.licence: Pixabay Content License: free use, modification allowed, no attribution required.
sources.restrictions: No sale or distribution of the content on a standalone basis (substantially unaltered); no commercial use of content with recognisable trademarks on goods; no misleading use of recognisable people; check third-party rights. => edited films only, never redistribute raw files.

imagery.name: USDA NAIP orthoimagery via USGS The National Map
imagery.credit: USDA FPAC / NAIP via USGS The National Map

imagery.name: USGS 3D Elevation Program (bare earth)
imagery.coverage: US, 1 m lidar where available, else 1/3 arc-second

imagery.licence: Copernicus Sentinel data: free, full and open, any use incl. commercial; attribution required
imagery.not: EOX Sentinel-2 cloudless is CC BY-NC-SA: never use

imagery.name: AWS Terrain Tiles (Mapzen terrarium)
imagery.coverage: global (SRTM 30 m, GMTED2010, ETOPO1, NED/3DEP in the US, EU-DEM, ...)
imagery.licence: Free; attribution of the underlying sources required
